fatal_errors: The proposed NiTi-Cu shape-memory alloy is unrelated to the target family of equiatomic FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived medium-entropy single crystals.

The hypothesis attributes temperature dependence to a martensitic phase transformation, whereas the target concerns dislocation glide through solid-solution obstacles, cryogenic inertial dulling, and high-temperature Portevin-Le Chatelier pinning.
It does not reconstruct the target compression geometry, slip system, 9–1373 K testing range, strain-rate jumps, CRSS analysis, TEM measurements, or MSAD calculations.
It conflates reversible shape-memory transformation strain with plastic deformation.
explanation: The response addresses temperature-dependent mechanical behavior only at a very broad level. Its material, intervention, phase-transformation mechanism, expected outcomes, and applicable conditions do not agree with the target study. The proposed DSC and temperature-dependent mechanical tests could discriminate the separate NiTi-Cu hypothesis, but they would not test the target mechanisms or reproduce its principal measurements. The idea is also a conventional NiTi-Cu alloying concept and is unsupported by cited evidence.
